drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is the main pregnancy-related problem: bleeding, pain, contractions, fluid leaking, the baby moving less, headache, or something else?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main obstetric complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: How far along are you, and have you had prenatal care and an ultrasound?
questions.rationale: Gestational age determines viability, ectopic risk, and which complications are likely.

questions.text: Have you had a positive pregnancy test, and do you know if this is an intrauterine pregnancy?
questions.rationale: An unconfirmed location leaves ectopic pregnancy on the table.

questions.text: Are you having vaginal bleeding, how heavy, and are you passing tissue or clots?
questions.rationale: Bleeding in pregnancy may be threatened miscarriage, ectopic, or later placental problems.

questions.text: Are you soaking pads hourly, feeling faint, or having shoulder pain with the bleeding?
questions.rationale: Heavy bleeding or syncope can indicate rupture or hemorrhage.

questions.text: Where is the pain, is it one-sided, crampy, or constant, and how severe?
questions.rationale: Unilateral pain early in pregnancy raises concern for ectopic pregnancy.

questions.text: Are you having regular tightening or contractions, how often, and does the belly stay hard?
questions.rationale: Regular contractions before term suggest preterm labor.

questions.text: Has fluid leaked from the vagina, is it a gush or trickle, and what color is it?
questions.rationale: Rupture of membranes changes infection and cord-prolapse risk.

questions.text: Have you felt the baby move less than usual?
questions.rationale: Reduced fetal movement needs urgent evaluation in the second half of pregnancy.

questions.text: Have you had a new severe headache, vision changes, or pain in the upper right belly?
questions.rationale: These are warning symptoms of preeclampsia and HELLP.

questions.text: Have you had sudden swelling of the face or hands, or high blood pressure readings?
questions.rationale: Sudden edema and hypertension support preeclampsia.

questions.text: Have you had a seizure, or felt about to have one?
questions.rationale: Seizure in pregnancy is eclampsia until proven otherwise.

questions.text: Have you had fever, burning urine, or foul discharge?
questions.rationale: Pyelonephritis and chorioamnionitis are obstetric emergencies.

questions.text: Have you had a fall, car accident, or has anyone hurt you?
questions.rationale: Trauma and intimate-partner violence are important in pregnancy.

questions.text: After injury, have you had bleeding, pain, or the baby moving less?
questions.rationale: Placental abruption can follow even modest trauma.

questions.text: Are you vomiting so much you cannot keep fluids down, or have you lost weight?
questions.rationale: Hyperemesis can cause dehydration and electrolyte problems.

questions.text: Have you had diabetes before pregnancy or gestational diabetes, and any very high or low sugars?
questions.rationale: Diabetes complications and DKA can occur in pregnancy.

questions.text: Have you had preterm birth, preeclampsia, C-section, miscarriage, or stillbirth before?
questions.rationale: Obstetric history is the strongest predictor of recurrence.

questions.text: Do you know your blood type, and have you received RhoGAM if you needed it?
questions.rationale: Rh status matters with bleeding.

questions.text: What medicines, prenatal vitamins, or substances are you taking, including alcohol or drugs?
questions.rationale: Teratogens, missed vitamins, and substances change risk.

questions.text: When was your last prenatal visit, and were there any problems with blood pressure, growth, or labs?
questions.rationale: Gaps in prenatal care and known complications frame urgency.

questions.text: Have you been told you have placenta previa, a low placenta, twins, or a short cervix?
questions.rationale: Known placental and cervical problems change bleeding and preterm-labor risk.

questions.text: Are you able to drink, walk, and feel the baby as expected, or do you feel too unwell?
questions.rationale: Functional status and fetal movement guide disposition.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Pregnancy with heavy bleeding, fainting, or shoulder pain
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report pregnancy or a positive test with heavy bleeding, fainting, or shoulder-tip pain?

red_flags.label: Baby moving less than usual
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report reduced fetal movement?

red_flags.label: Headache, vision change, or upper abdominal pain in pregnancy
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report new severe headache, vision changes, or right-upper-belly pain in pregnancy?

red_flags.label: Seizure in pregnancy
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a seizure while pregnant?

red_flags.label: Regular contractions or fluid leak before term
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report regular contractions or leaking fluid before 37 weeks?

red_flags.label: Trauma with bleeding or reduced movement
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a fall or blow to the belly with bleeding, pain, or less fetal movement?
